shortlist.label: Atrial Fibrillation
shortlist.why_kept: Irregular narrow complex tachycardia on ECG with atrial rate of 210 bpm

shortlist.label: Atrial Flutter
shortlist.why_kept: Significant transmitral flow variations on echocardiography and irregular heart rhythm

shortlist.label: Constrictive Pericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: History of pulmonary tuberculosis and jugular venous pressure with a prominent y descent

shortlist.label: Restrictive Cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Biatrial dilatation and grade III diastolic dysfunction on echocardiography

shortlist.label: Cardiac Amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: History of metastatic bladder carcinoma and signs of cardiac dysfunction

raw.rationale: The ECG shows an irregular narrow complex tachycardia with a ventricular rate of 78 bpm and an atrial rate of 210 bpm, which is consistent with atrial flutter. The inverted P-wave morphology in the inferior limb leads also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Atrial Fibrillation
rejected.why: Atrial fibrillation typically presents with an irregularly irregular rhythm, whereas the ECG in this case shows a regular atrial rate of 210 bpm.

rejected.label: Constrictive Pericarditis
rejected.why: Constrictive pericarditis would likely present with signs of right heart failure, such as elevated jugular venous pressure, but the prominent y descent in this case is more suggestive of restrictive cardiomyopathy or cardiac amyloidosis.

rejected.label: Restrictive Cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: While the echocardiography shows biatrial dilatation and grade III diastolic dysfunction, which could be seen in restrictive cardiomyopathy, the ECG findings are more consistent with atrial flutter.

rejected.label: Cardiac Amyloidosis
rejected.why: Cardiac amyloidosis can present with restrictive cardiomyopathy-like features, but the ECG findings in this case are more specific for atrial flutter.
